author: Sarai Bennett
title: New details emerge after HVAC tech's deadly shooting - NewsBreak
text:
By Sarai Bennett ,
11 hours ago MEMPHIS, Tenn. -- New details have been released after a man was accused of shooting his co-worker in the face while working in a Midtown neighborhood Tuesday morning.
Ashton Williams, 21, is charged with Voluntary Manslaughter, Possession of a Firearm During the Commission of a Dangerous Felony, Theft of Property Less Than $2,500, and Possession of a Controlled Substance with the Intent to Manufacture/Deliver/Sell, to wit: Marijuana.
Williams' bond is set at $275,000. He was arraigned in court Wednesday morning, and said he did not have an attorney. He will be back in court for a bond hearing Thursday.
Ashton Williams (SCSO) ORIGINAL STORY: Man charged in deadly shooting of co-worker On Tuesday, officers say they responded to a shooting call in the 1000 block of Roland Street.
Police said Williams called them, saying he shot his co-worker.
When they arrived at the scene, they found a man lying on the sidewalk, suffering from a gunshot wound.
He was taken to Regional One, where he later died from his injuries. Police identified the victim as Larry Swindle.
According to MPD, authorities spoke with a resident in the neighborhood who told them that he called Choate's Heating and Cooling to come to his home for service.
The man said he heard Williams and Swindle arguing, followed by a "pop noise."
When he came outside, the man stated that he saw Swindle had been shot and that Williams told him he had shot him.
FedEx St. Jude Championship to lose status on PGA Tour after 2027 While police were at the scene, they said they recovered a black handgun and a cartridge casing. Investigators say the firearm was reported stolen from a vehicle in Southaven, MS.
Officers also said they located a backpack in the front passenger's side floorboard containing marijuana.
Williams was taken into custody.
As he was being questioned, investigators said Williams told them that he and Swindle were involved in a verbal altercation while doing HVAC work inside the home.
Williams allegedly said he and Swindle went outside and around the corner from the home, and that's when Swindle punched him in the face.
MPD said Williams and Swindle got into a physical altercation, and during the fight, Swindle wrapped his arm around Williams's neck and made threats to him.
Eventually, the fight ended, and Williams walked back to the Choates work van to sit in the front passenger seat.
Williams then told investigators that Swindle walked up to the van, balling his fist as if he was going to hit him again while making threats.
Williams pulled out his gun and shot Swindle one time, detectives stated.
WREG reached out to Choate's for comment, and we are waiting to hear back.
Those who live nearby say this incident should not have resulted in gun violence.
“That violence got transported here through some workers. This is an elementary school, a really good one right there, Rozelle Elementary. There's some good people on this street,” said Gerald Harris, Midtown resident.
“The man that had a gun, shouldn't have had a gun. Don't nobody need a gun. And the way they got the system now, they shouldn't let anybody have a gun,” said Antonio Watson, Midtown resident.
